sentences.text: The holotype skull measures 57.2 cm from the front of the premaxilla to the back of the quadrate.
A specific hole along the bottom edge of the jaw contact point is missing in every known specimen.
Bones named the quadratojugal and squamosal form a long flange in this animal.
Fossils were found in the United States, specifically within the Lance and Hell Creek formations of Montana and Wyoming.
The species was described by Sancarlo and Paul.
Researchers suggest that the long hind legs indicate a lifestyle adapted for chasing prey rather than ambush hunting.
Estimates suggest the animal had a maximum running speed of 12.57 to 13.82 m/s, nearly twice that of an adult T. rex.
Healed puncture wounds on the holotype specimen suggest it survived an attack by another juvenile tyrannosaur.
The genus Nanotyrannus was established by Bakker, Currie, and Williams in 1988, with the type species Nanotyrannus lancensis originally described by Gilmore in 1946.
A recent study by Zanno and Napoli in 2025 designated Nanotyrannus lethaeus as the type species for Gilmoretyrannus.
This animal lived in western North America during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 67 million years ago, or between 68 and 66 million years ago.
The taxonomic status of Nanotyrannus has been a subject of intense scientific debate, with many researchers favoring its identification as a juvenile Tyrannosaurus rex.
An independent study by Griffin et al. argued the holotype skull belonged to a mature individual based on hyoid bone histology, but this methodology was questioned by Woodruff et al. in 2026.

Specimens possess 15-16 teeth on the upper jaw and 16-18 on the lower jaw, while adults have fewer; paleontologist Carr hypothesized the difference was due to growth patterns seen in Gorgosaurus libratus.
